The Edge of Darkness Trilogy #2

Voracious

Leigh Rivers

4.31

'Filled with TENSION, HEARTBREAK and ELECTRIC CHEMISTRY. This one will tear your heart right out of your chest before tossing it back in and sewing you up' No. 1 New York Times bestselling author Brynne Weaver

'Leigh Rivers is THE QUEEN OF DARK ROMANCE. Her books are deeply emotive and her characters feel so vividly real' Tierney Page

He'll never forget her, but he'll never forgive her either . . .

Now back home with the security of Kade's team, Stacey is pulled further into her own living hell, desperate for a chance to escape - until the opportunity finally comes to fight back.

Kade has never been so deep in the pits of hell itself. Seeing Stacey once nearly knocked him off his axis but seeing her twice - ready to make amends and fix the past - is a disaster waiting to happen.

Yet, despite his hatred for her, she's his anchor; the memories of what they used to be the only thing keeping him sane and preventing the darkness from consuming him. But what happens when the truth about their past finally unravels, and he learns what really happened the night that tore them apart?

Voracious is a dark romance and contains explicit sexual content and difficult themes. Please read the content warnings before reading. Recommended 18+.

About the author

Leigh Rivers

19 books21.8k followers
Leigh Rivers is a Scottish Biomedical Scientist who has ventured into the world of writing dark, morally gray characters with rollercoaster storylines to drive her readers wild.

When she isn't reading, writing on her laptop, or gaming until ridiculous hours, she dances at the pole studio, goes to the gym, and walks her four dogs with her two sons and husband.

"I choose who I love, and I choose you."

Stopp this was everything and definitely not for the fainthearted. Going in, I was aware that this is darker than Insatiable but I hadn't expected the level of dark I was going to be met with. It's definitely not the sort of read you can binge in a single read. I had to take so many pauses to just process, cry and feel the pain.

The author does a brilliant job at making this book and its love and pain seem realistic. Midst of all the chaos, the darkness and everything going wrong, the simple truth remains: Kade and Stacey love each other. And despite them being separated from each other for the majority of the book, you don't really question that love. That sort of love is presented as absolute and undeniable.

I love Kade and Stacey so much, they deserve so much happiness. Like poor babies haven't had a moment of joy, stability and peace in their lives and for once I would like to see that part of them. Tobias is someone I adore. Like sure he's a diagnosed psychopath but he's a pookie bear too 🥺👉👈 I wanna see more of him in the next one. Base and Luciella have me nervous I won't lie 😩😩 I feel bad and heartbroken for Base in particular.

I can't wait for some justice to be done after all the trauma. I can't wait to see some of the sickos in this book dead in the next book. Brooo this one was such a heavy read, I'm gonna need to take a bit of a time to process this before I start book three. The cliffhanger is really good and tempts me to read book three but I'm gonna be a sobbing mess if I pick it up right now 😭

~•~•~

I miss Kade and I hear this one is an even more of an intense emotional rollercoaster? Well, here I go.

"Look at me now, little princess. Daddy's gone, and he's never coming back."


believe it or not, i've been trying to write this review for HOURS. so far all i've been able to do is write a few paragraphs, think about chapter 26, cry again, stare at the wall blankly for a few minutes and delete everything. rinse and repeat.
you won't believe me but i made a 12 page long word document while rereading this book. 12 pages, over 4k words, and yet i find myself at an impasse because i still don't know how to review this book without spoiling anything (so naturally, spoilers will be marked because i need to get some things off my chest before i fully spiral). like yes, this book made me physically sick. it fucking obliterated me emotionally. it devastated me and bared my soul. and i wouldn't have it any other way.
it's not just a book that you only read. it's a story that you need to experience head on (but please please check your triggers because it gets really really dark and painful).
it's all just so heartbreaking. i don't think there was even a single chapter where i did not have tears in my eyes. it's so painful and it really broke me. i need the author to pay for my therapy rn.
honestly, i really don't know how i was able to read this trilogy in one sitting the first time i read it. because when kade got to know the truth and he was forced to see the video of it, i had to put the book down. i couldn't do it. reading that scene made me physically sick and nauseous. i had to stop reading and put the book down for an hour or two and take a nap before i could even stomach picking it up again.
this book was just 39 chapters of sheer heartbreak and pain. rinse and repeat. all over again. leigh does not pull any punches (as expected) and it's heartbreaking, really (if i had a penny for the amount of times i've written heartbreaking, or painful in my notes😭)
this book seamlessly picks up from where insatiable left off. like i've already said b4, insatiable gave us mere snippets of the impending devastation to come. but this book? this is where the real devastation fully strikes in. the plot deepens, the characters feel so very real (albeit broken), horrible horrible things happen and the truth comes out and the stakes have never been higher.


Kade in the flashbacks was so sweet, insecure and shy, who used to overthink everything. the changes in him are so drastic but also very expected, considering all that he's been through.
and stacey? oh god i don't think she's given enough credit for her resilience. after all she went through, she did NOT give up. though there were many occasions when she was tempted to but she did NOT.
kade and stacey. stacey and kade. my shaylaaaaas😭😭😭😭
my heart breaks for them. it's genuinely very shocking how much i'm attached to these two. every single flashback had me clutching my chest because IT HURT SO MUCH. AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHKJGHJSHFHGHHHHHH.
my mini freak out session aside, i just want them to be happy again. these two just can't seem to get a break. jeez. i just want them happy and together. oh god.
this book also has side characters who feel so real and with insane depth. commendable, really. i felt so attached to the side characters- tobias, barry and base. lu did something that did NOT sit right with me. so i'm really conflicted but i'm hoping that she redeems herself in the last book but more on that later in the spoilers section. also, what really surprised me was how much i liked aria in this book (she got on my nerves A LOT when i was reading psychotic obsession lol).
also it's an EoD review. how can it be complete without a tobias mitchell appreciation section mhm🫦( okay stop you're being too much ). anyway. if you know me, you probably know that i'm obsessed with tobias mitchell (pun not intended lol) call him unhinged, toxic or a psycho (all true btw) but you can't deny that tobias with his children is mhmmmmm🫦🫦🫦( stop you're doing it again ). jokes aside, i really can't wait to see more of him in book 3. those scenes with kade (ifykyk) mhmm>>>>
after all, what can i say i'm just a simple girl who looooves a good revenge arc. more on that in the spoilers section hehehehe.

chris, archie, bernadette, cassie can go to hell for all i care. i hate them sm it's not even funny. and no, i won't waste my words more than i already have on these disgusting pigs.

okayyy so i have sooo many things that i need to get off my chest before i spiral so bear with me.
so kade and stacey BOTH were raped (and gangraped) they have been through SO MUCH hell and neither of them deserved any of the brutalities that were thrown in their life. my heart breaks sm for them. they were expecting a child- a girl. and they had so many dreams. kade's father is tobias mitchell, who's a psychopath who struggles to come terms with reality if his meds are taken away from him. tobias hurt aria when they were younger (and that's an understatement. by hurt, i meant that he also kidnapped and drugged her). they were toxic. so that's also a thing that kade feared would happen. he used to be so afraid that he would also get obsessed with stacey, and that he might hurt her the way tobias hurt aria. we can definitely see some traits of tobias in kade. but he's not as deep into psychosis as tobias was. kade in the flashbacks was so sweet and shy and insecure and an overthinker. the changes in him were DRASTIC. he used to say that he'd never touch a gun in his life ever because he needs stacey's parents' approval and he already has enough of a bad reputation as it is.
i first read this series a few months ago. and my problem with majority of book 1 and some parts of book 2 when i first read it was that kade and stacey barely spend any time together in the present timeline (the story's told in dual timeline) and whenever they do, they spend the whole chapter doing it. while rereading, i had an epiphany. lmao not really.
okay so it was mentioned once in this book and that just stayed with me. archie and bernadette have been abusing kade for years. he's getting raped from the age of 19. for 3-4 years. they drug him and force him and sell him to "clients" and use him as some sort of murder machine? they drug him so much so that sometimes he's completely out of his senses. and there's a permanent damage to his hand. tremors. in one of the chapters, it was mentioned and i quote "But I understand. १˒🪄⋆ stacey rhodes. the absolute shit (for lack of better words) that she went through in this book & insatiable were just traumitizing. she’s such a strong and resilient character that keeps fighting back no matter what - which i really admired. 90% of the dark romance fmc's that i’ve read about have been doormats - no, airplane runways. lola king fmc’s would bow at her feet. stacey would own them i fear. even though she’s getting she’s still considering everyone’s feelings around her, which was just. please girl, worry about yourself and YOUR life/livelihood. you think you’re a people pleaser until you read about ms. stacey rhodes. the end shocked me and i’m not prepared to see what she goes through in the third book.

𖥨⭒˚ kade mitchell. oh my heart. i’ve never vehemently hated villains in the dark romance world as much as i hate bernadette, her daughter, archie, and chris. he went through so much in his life and watching him go through this horror film was so hard to read about. many of the scenes where i had to physically put the book down was when he was getting . him and stacey deserve the most beautiful happy ending ever. i was bombarding mads with messages and something that repeatedly came up with was how we both are yearning for their cutesy moments where they are safe and happy together.

side charcters. ᝰ.ᐟ this part will contain spoilers!!

- this series is ADDICTIVE. suddenly 60% is over in one day

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ 4.5 stars (rounded up)

I absolutely devoured this book. It was so devastating, and at this point I am completely invested in Stacey and Kade.

Leigh Rivers took everything that worked in Insatiable and turned the volume all the way up—higher stakes, darker tension, sharper twists, and a story that completely refuses to let you breathe. This isn’t just spicy or shocking for the sake of it; it’s layered, intense, and emotionally gripping in a way that kept me glued to the pages.

What really stood out was how much the plot deepened. The world feels richer, the characters more complex, and the relationships more unhinged in the best possible way. Every reveal felt earned, every moment of tension landed, and the pacing was relentless. I kept thinking, okay, surely it can’t get more unhinged than this—and then it did.

The character work is phenomenal: messy, morally gray, obsessive, and raw—exactly how I want my dark romance characters to be. I especially love Kade’s soft spot for Stacey, children, and dogs 🥹. The emotional pull surprised me just as much as the intensity, and by the end I was fully feral, emotionally compromised, and already desperate for what comes next. I could not put this book down toward the end, and that ending absolutely shook me.

Highly recommend if you have a taste for dark romance—but definitely check the trigger warnings, because this book gets DARK.

Like yes, on one side I feel really bad for them and what they are going through, both individually and together, but on the other side, when they are together, all they do is fuck. It got annoying after like the 4th time. I had a box of tissues next to me because I thought I was going to sob, but I didn't use a single one. Instead, I got the ick with these two. I have to admit I did skim a little here and there, especially when it came to Kade and Stacey.

Honestly, Tobias, Base and Luciella are my only motivation for this trilogy. Onto to the third (and final) book.
